exposure: Prolonged latent phase of labour (defined as 18 hours or more)
outcome: Prevalence of prolonged latent phase of labour
cohort: 1343 women who intended vaginal births and who had spontaneous onset of labour at 37 or more weeks' gestation at a mid-sized hospital in western Sweden during a one-year period (2013-2014).
finding: Women with a prolonged latent phase of labour were more likely to receive obstetric interventions, including amniotomy, augmentation of labour, instrumental vaginal birth, and emergency caesarean section.
